correctness.rationale: The line-graph translation is exact: the selected edges must be connected on their positive-degree vertices; domination is equivalent to covering a whole shore, because any pair of uncovered vertices across the shores yields an undominated rook. Removing a cycle edge preserves both properties. A spanning tree covering both full shores admits a leaf deletion preserving one full shore. For a tree covering only one full shore, leaves on the opposite occupied shore are removable; if there are none, every pendant-edge deletion loses a vertex of the full shore and every other edge deletion separates two nonempty edge sets. A proper connected dominating subset could be enlarged along adjacency to a one-deletion set, so this deletion test establishes inclusion-minimality. The weighted bipartite tree identity gives words of lengths j−1 and m−1; the second must use all j column labels, giving j! times the Stirling number. The degree bound j≤m−1 and proper coverage j<n give exactly the stated range. The transpose is disjoint. Positivity of the summands gives the two intervals, the gap at n≥2m, and the stated extremal multiplicities, including ties for squares and the two-row boundary. The accompanying graph-vertex checker and recorded nine-board histogram are finite supporting evidence and were inspected, not executed.
